To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the first planar chiral P,S-bidentated ligand based on the (eta5-cp)(eta4-cod) cobalt core has been prepared and that this ligand shows high efficiency and enantioselectivity in Pd-c-catalyzed reactions.

the new planar chiral cobalt complex (R)-[Cp*PPh2SbCo(eta4-tetraPhC4)] (R-1) is an excellent chiral ligand for Pd-catalysed allylic substitutions, with a high level of enantioselectivity and high activity in a wide range of substrates.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new chiral ligands for asymmetric catalysis and with the study of the mechanism of the catalyzed reaction in order to understand how the chiral information is transmitted to the product.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of this ligand in the Pd-catalysis of asymmetric allylic substitutions is the first example of a P,S-ligand based on a planar chiral cyclopentadienone backbone.
the use of the planar chirality in the Pd-catalytic system allows the enantioselectivities to be increased by a factor of 3.
the use of the planar-chiral ligand in P,S-bidentation mode is the best choice in terms of enantiomeric excesses and reaction rates.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a planar chiral cobalt cyclopentadienide as P,S-bisligand in Pd(0)-catalyzed allylations allows us to obtain the corresponding products with very high levels of enantioselectivity, even with a low catalyst loading.
the use of a chiral cobalt complex as P,S-donor ligand in P,S-Pd catalysis can be an efficient alternative to the use of a planar chiral phosphine ligand.

the use of a planar chiral ligand based on an (eta5-cp)(eta4-cbd) Co backbone is an efficient strategy to obtain high enantiomeric excess in the allylic substitution of racemic 1,3-diphenylprop-2-yl acetate.
